taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-24, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1101.7 | 4.18 | 4.18
2 | 1144.4 | 12.44 | 16.62
3 | 549.8 | 0.62 | 17.24
4 | 173.3 | 7.65 | 24.89
5 | 2079.8 | 25.05 | 49.94
6 | 1111.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KQHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-24, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-24 in Survey Area T shows a six-layer subsurface profile. The resistivity sequence begins at 1101.7 ohm-m, increases slightly in Layer 2, and then decreases significantly through Layers 3 and 4, reaching a minimum of 173.3 ohm-m. A high-resistivity layer (2079.8 ohm-m) is encountered at Layer 5, followed by a decrease in Layer 6. The resulting curve type is KQHK, which aligns perfectly with the station's classification on file. The interpreted model reaches a depth of approximately 50 meters.

{"curve_type_stated": "KQHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
